source.author: lucan
source.text: Non chalybem gentes penitus fugiente metallo Eruerent, nulli vallarent oppida muri, Non sonipes in bella ferox, non iret in aequor Turrigeras classis pelago sparsura carinas, Si bene libertas umquam pro pace daretur.
source.text_original: Non chalybem gentes penitus fugiente metallo / Eruerent, nulli vallarent oppida muri, / Non sonipes in bella ferox, non iret in aequor / Turrigeras classis pelago sparsura carinas, / Si bene libertas umquam pro pace daretur.
source.text_english: No nations would dig up iron, if the metal were wholly fleeing away; no walls would fortify cities with ramparts; no warhorse would be fierce for battle; no fleet would go out upon the sea with towers on its ships, scattering its battlements across the deep, if liberty were ever rightly granted in place of peace.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: securus in aequor haut minus Erginus, proles Neptunia, fertur, qui maris insidias, clarae qui sidera noctis norit et e clausis quem destinet Aeolus antris, non metuat cui regna ratis, cui tradere caelum assidua Tiphys vultum lassatus ab Arcto.
reuse.text_original: securus in aequor / haut minus Erginus, proles Neptunia, fertur, / qui maris insidias, clarae qui sidera noctis / norit et e clausis quem destinet Aeolus antris, / non metuat cui regna ratis, cui tradere caelum / assidua Tiphys vultum lassatus ab Arcto.
reuse.text_english: Secure, into the sea is borne Erginus, no less so, a child of Neptune, one who knows the sea’s ambushes, one who knows the stars of the clear night and whom Aeolus dispatches from his closed caves, who need not fear the ship’s dominion, to whom Tiphys, worn out by constant watch, wishes to entrust the sky, steering from the North.
